key_insight: Strain-space hyperreduction extends EMSL, ECM, and E3C to large-deformation solid mechanics with boundary conditions enforced by construction, improving runtime-accuracy tradeoffs over displacement-space ECSW.
engineering_relevance: This enables much faster nonlinear solid simulations for parameterized materials and deformations, supporting reduced-order analysis and design workflows with minimal loss of accuracy.
method: Build boundary-consistent lifting fields offline to satisfy arbitrary Dirichlet conditions.
Formulate Empirical Cubature Method, E3C, and EMSL directly in strain space.
Compare strain-space hyperreduction methods against displacement-space ECSW on hyperelastic benchmarks.
evidence_signal: On two hyperelastic test problems, the strain-space methods outperformed displacement-space ECSW; EMSL reached about 100,000× speedup and E3C about 10,000× speedup while maintaining high accuracy.
watch_item: Offline basis construction and cubature selection add preprocessing cost, so the best method depends on whether the application can afford more offline work or needs the fastest online evaluation.
paper_title: Efficient strain-space hyperreduction in large-deformation solid mechanics
